args.sql: SELECT maintregistry, maintcostusd, cleancostusd, replacecostusd, revlossusd, inspectres, wtystatus FROM maintenance LIMIT 20;

SELECT 
  MIN(maintcostusd) as min_maint, MAX(maintcostusd) as max_maint,
  MIN(cleancostusd) as min_clean, MAX(cleancostusd) as max_clean,
  MIN(replacecostusd) as min_replace, MAX(replacecostusd) as max_replace,
  MIN(revlossusd) as min_revloss, MAX(revlossusd) as max_revloss
FROM maintenance;

SELECT 
  maintregistry,
  maintcostusd + cleancostusd + replacecostusd as total_cost,
  revlossusd,
  CASE WHEN (maintcostusd + cleancostusd + replacecostusd) > 0 
    THEN revlossusd / (maintcostusd + cleancostusd + replacecostusd)
    ELSE NULL 
  END as cost_efficiency_score
FROM maintenance 
ORDER BY cost_efficiency_score ASC 
LIMIT 10;

result: The "maintenance cost score" is calculated by summing the maintenance, cleaning, and replacement costs and then dividing by the plant's generation capacity in megawatts (GenCapMW). The query is intended to DELETE records where this score exceeds 290, indicating poor cost efficiency.

args.sql:
SELECT 
  m.maintregistry,
  m.maintcostusd, m.cleancostusd, m.replacecostusd,
  p.gencapmw,
  (m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) / p.gencapmw as cost_score
FROM maintenance m
JOIN plant p ON m.powerref = p.growregistry
WHERE (m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) / p.gencapmw > 290
LIMIT 10;

DELETE FROM maintenance
WHERE maintregistry IN (
  SELECT m.maintregistry
  FROM maintenance m
  JOIN plant p ON m.powerref = p.growregistry
  WHERE (m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) / p.gencapmw > 290
);
